We provide a caring and friendly environment where every child is supported to develop strong skills, creativity, and a lifelong love of learning.
Headteacher’s Welcome
Greatfields Primary School is a small mixed community school which is based in Barking within the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham. We are fortunate to be housed in a fabulous modern building which boasts large class rooms that provide a clean and spacious environment for our children to learn in. We pride ourselves on providing a caring and friendly atmosphere associated with smaller schools. Your child’s time at Greatfields Primary School is very precious and we are pleased that we are able to share this with you. We provide a curriculum that acknowledges the importance of the basic skills, but endeavours to teach those skills in an exciting way, as well as finding time to focus on more creative and artistic skills and making sure that we enjoy what we learn, using our local and wider environments and opportunities to support this.
Mrs Nawaz-Stevens Headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: School Values & Ethos  | Greatfields Primary School
pageCache.text:
School Values & Ethos
We want to develop a school culture in which every student has the highest of aspirations for themselves and are encouraged to fulfil this aspiration by their teachers and parents. Our School should be a place in which staff and students from all backgrounds, religions and cultures can thrive and be challenged every day.
Learning is the key to unlocking a child’s potential and our job as teachers is to inspire our students in class every day and to imbue in them a love for and expertise in each subject. Alongside this, our students will have the opportunity to learn new skills and to develop interests they never knew they had.
The partnership between the school and our parents is fundamental in ensuring that we achieve this. We want to work alongside our parents in order to ensure the best possible outcomes for all of our students.
Our core values can be summarised as RESPECT –
We encourage children to take ownership of, and responsibility for, their learning and behaviour. We aim for our children to fulfil their potential and shape their future.
Resilience
Self- belief
Perseverance
Courageous

About Us
Welcome to Greatfields Primary School.
Thank you for visiting our website. We are pleased to provide you with an overview of our esteemed school.
Greatfields Primary is a small, mixed Free School that is part of the Partnership Learning Multi-Academy Trust, located in Barking, within the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham. We are fortunate to occupy a modern, purpose-built facility featuring spacious classrooms, which offer a clean and conducive learning environment for our pupils. We take great pride in fostering a nurturing and supportive atmosphere, which is characteristic of smaller schools.
We highly value the time your child spends at Greatfields Primary School, and we are delighted to be part of their educational journey. Our curriculum is designed to emphasise the importance of fundamental skills, while also delivering them in an engaging and stimulating manner. Additionally, we dedicate time to promoting creativity and artistic expression, ensuring that our pupils not only learn but also enjoy the process, utilising both our local and broader environments as part of their learning experience.
Our staff is fully committed to the effective inclusion of children with a diverse range of educational needs and abilities. We are proud of our dedicated team of teachers and support staff, who strive every day to ensure that every child achieves their full potential.
We invite you to explore our website to learn more about our school. Should you be a prospective parent or member of the community, we warmly encourage you to visit us in person. Either I or a member of our team would be delighted to provide you with a tour of our facilities.
Mrs Nawaz-Stevens- Head of School

Breakfast & After School Club
Greatfields Primary School are very pleased to be offering a Breakfast Club every morning.
Early Morning Breakfast Club:
Breakfast Club begins at 7.30am every morning and the last parent drop off time is 8.00am. Breakfast is free however, there is a £2 daily charge per child to cover the cost of childcare for your child.
We offer a nutritional breakfast consisting of:
Children are provided with the opportunity to play board games, read or socialise with their friends during their time at Breakfast Club.

Greatfields School and Greatfields Primary School – Subcommittees Structure
The Local Governing Board, (LGB) is responsible for the Greatfields School (secondary) and the Greatfields Primary School which opened in September 2024. This is not a through school structure.
The LGB is supported and serviced by 4 subcommittees, independently clerked and comprising members of the LGB, the Headteachers and Executive leadership of both schools. Members of the Senior Leadership Teams (SLT) attend as appropriate.
The Sub-Committees are:
Greatfields Primary School opened in September 2024 with a single year group. Coordinated arrangements for governance are in place between the two schools as follows:
Finance, Operations and Audit (Secondary and Primary)
Pay and Personnel (Secondary)
1. Safeguarding, Student Experience, Curriculum and Standards (secondary)
Scope for Safeguarding and Student Experience aspect (Secondary)
a) Student Safeguarding (SG)
e) Vulnerable students across the school
g) Community Relations
h) Personal Development Curriculum
i) Student Opportunities and achievements
j) Alternative Provision (AP)
Scope for Curriculum and Standards aspect (Secondary)
a) The breadth and balance of the curriculum
b) Oversight of assessment arrangements
c) Monitoring and review of examination results
d) Provision made for SEND
f) Preparations made for progression / later life
g) The impact of Pupil Premium Grant funding
A parallel subcommittee structure is in place with Greatfields Primary School
2. Curriculum, Standards and Safeguarding (Primary)
Scope for this Committee
This sub-committee considers:
a) The breadth and balance of the curriculum
b) Oversight of assessment arrangements
c) Provision made for SEND
e) The impact of Pupil Premium Grant funding
3. Finance, Operations and Audit Committee (Secondary and Primary)
Scope for this Committee
a) Financial management for both schools
b) Audit of both schools
c) Deployment of capital and other resources for both schools
d) Risk management for both schools
e) Health and safety for both schools
4. Pay and Personnel (Secondary)
Scope for this Committee
a) HR Matters and related policies and guidance
b) Staff Personnel issues and related policies and guidance
c) Pay Policy and related guidance
e) Review and amend the policies which come under its remit.
f) To enable governors to meet their duty of care of the staff of the school
g) Recruitment, redundancies and restructure of school staff
h) Training and professional development
i) Staff work life-balance, and well-being
k) Staff discipline grievances, and capability.
l) Whistleblowing process and policy
Matters relating to the primary school will be dealt with as need arises and with the growth in the school an appropriate accountability structure will be agreed and implanted.
